title: Unit Circle Definition
text: $$\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)$$ represents the y-coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{4\pi}{3}.$$\n##figure4.gif##

title: Reference Angle
text: The reference angle for $$\frac{4\pi}{3}$$ is $$\frac{\pi}{3}.$$ The absolute values of the coordinates are given by the legs of a $$30-60-90$$ triangle with hypotenuse $$1$$. The $$x-$$ coordinate is $$\frac{1}{2}.$$ The $$y-$$ coordinate is obtained from the Pythagorean theorem: $$\sqrt{1**2-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)**2}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$\n##figure5.gif##

title: Quadrant Sign
text: The angle $$\frac{4\pi}{3}$$ is in the third quadrant, where y-coordinates are negative. Therefore, $$\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$\n##figure6.gif##
